Civil Miscellaneous Appeal filed under Section 173 of the
 Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the Award dated 17.07.2023 in

For Appellants : Mr.U.Chithambaram
 R1 : No appearance

 Judgment
The appellants are the claimants in M.C.O.P. 2240 of 2021 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Small Causes Court, Chennai.

sentences.text:
They filed the claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation of Rs.49,00,000/- for the death of one Pankaj Chouhan,
(son of claimant 1 and brother of claimants 2 and 3) in a road accident that occurred on 11.04.2021.

2. The brief case of the appellants / claimants is as follows :
On 11.04.2021, Pankaj Chouhan (since deceased) was riding his motorcycle bearing Registration Number TN-18-Q-8346 on Ponneri - https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Chennai Highways.

When he was nearing Manali Pudhu Nagar, a container lorry bearing Registration Number TN-28-BE-7509 was parked on the main road without any indicator or signal, as a result of which, the two wheeler driven by Pankaj Chouhan hit the lorry and was ran over by another container lorry bearing Registration Number TN-20-BR-8850.
He died on spot.

3. According to the claimants, the negligent parking of the container lorry bearing Registration Number TN-28-BE-7509 on the road and rash and negligent driving of the driver of the another container lorry bearing Registration Number TN-20-BR-8850 were the cause of the accident.
Since the said vehicles were insured with the respondents 2 and 4, the owners and their respective insurers are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to them.
4. In the Tribunal the owners of the two container lorries remained absent and were set ex parte.
The respondents 2 and 4 resisted the claim petition on all the grounds available to the insurer under Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 5.

The Tribunal, vide its orders dated 17.07.2023, fastened negligence on the part of the drivers of the container lorries bearing Registration Numbers TN-28-BE-7509 and TN-20-BR-8850 in the ratio 50:50 and also held that the owners of the vehicles and their respective insurers are jointly and Shyamlal vs Sri Sodambikai Transport on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77630168/
2 severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.8,91,800/- each (50% of the total compensation of Rs.17,83,600/-) to the first claimant together with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of the petition till the date of realisation.

The Tribunal dismissed the claim petition as against the claimants 2 and 3.
6.
Aggrieved over the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimants have filed the present appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

7. Heard Mr.U.Chithambaram, learned counsel appearing for the appellants and Ms.G.Sukumari,
learned counsel appearing for the second respondent.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 8.
Mr.U.Chithambaram, learned counsel appearing for the appellants contended that Pankaj Chouhan (since deceased) was working in a private concern earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
However, the Tribunal fixed the notional monthly income of the deceased only as Rs.12,000/-, which, according to him, is very meagre.
He therefore, prayed for enhancement of the notional monthly income of the deceased.

9. Per contra Ms.G.Sukumari, learned counsel appearing for the second respondent contended that the Award passed by the Tribunal is based on the well laid down principles of law which were in vogue at the time of passing of the order and therefore, the same need not be disturbed at this stage.
10. A perusal of the records shows that Pankaj Chouhan (since deceased) was a graduate in Bachelor of Business Administration (B.B.A.) and was working in a private concern as a System Admin.
According to the claimants, his monthly income was Rs.20,000/-.
In the absence of https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis satisfactory income proof, the Tribunal fixed the notional monthly income of the deceased as Rs.12,000/-.
The accident took place in the year 2021 and the deceased was aged 28 years on the date of accident.
In the circumstances, this Court is of the opinion that fixing notional monthly income of the deceased at Rs.18,000/- would meet the ends of justice.
As per the decision of the Supreme Court of India in National Insurance Co. vs Pranay sethi and others reported in 2017 (2) TNMAC 601, 40% is added towards future prospects of the deceased.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. vs Pranay sethi and others reported in 2017 (2) TNMAC 601
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The deceased died as a bachelor and hence, 50% is deducted towards his personal expenses.

The proper multiplier to be adopted in the instant case is 17 as per the decision rendered in Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121.
Calculation Notional Monthly Income = Rs.18,000/-
40% Future Prospects = Rs.25,200/-
After 1/2 deduction = Rs.12,600/-
Loss of dependency = Rs.12,600/- x 12 x 17 = Rs.25,70,400/-

No costs.
